transcript:
Header: 2026-12-01 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~60 min | Attendees: Alex, Priya, Marcus, Sofia, Lena, Tom, Elena, Raj
[00:00] Alex Johnson: alright folks, thanks for joining, we got an hour for this enablement, main goals are messaging, competitor calls, and demo practice. um, Priya will run a demo later.
[00:28] Priya Patel: hey everyone, hi. quick note, if the transcript sounds off sometimes it's because the auto transcriber messes up acronyms like KV cache or K M S, so ignore that.
[00:46] Lena Ortiz: perfect, yes, we want crisp one-liners we can coach AEs on. start with the 30-second pitch.
[01:05] Alex Johnson: ok 30-sec pitch attempt: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLMs predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Emphasize predictable latency and cost. feedback?
[01:34] Tom Nguyen: i like predictable, can we put more emphasis on the fallback story? customers ask about reliability when GPUs fill up.
[01:52] Marcus Chen: yes mention smart routing + automatic fallback to compatible model variants. also talk about KV caching and prefix caching — sometimes transcribed as K V cash — so say "prefix cache" in plain words.
[02:20] Priya Patel: competitive quickcalls: vs OpenAI — focus on deployment modes (we do private and dedicated with SLAs), vs Anthropic — focus on performance per dollar and kernel optimizations, vs Bedrock — emphasize unified runtime across environments and production tooling.
[03:00] Elena Park: question: when customers ask about SOC2 and encryption, what's the short answer?
[03:15] Alex Johnson: short answer: we have SOC 2 readiness, enterprise Private supports KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, RBAC, and we can run in customer VPC or on-prem. longer answers available in security one-pager we'll share.
[03:42] Raj Singh: also mention data residency and retention options for regulated customers.
[04:00] Priya Patel: ok moving to demo script — we'll do a 10-minute flow, starting from API call (text generation + function/tool call), show streaming, then show latency numbers and a failover to a cheaper model.
[04:30] Alex Johnson: callout: when you show latency, frame token cost and latency tradeoffs. say something like "we optimize for predictable p99 latency while offering batching and quantization levers to lower unit cost".
[05:00] Tom Nguyen: on quantization — how deep do AEs need to get? customers sometimes ask "can you quantize without losing quality?"
[05:20] Marcus Chen: keep it simple: we recommend model/quantization profiles per workload; our Optimize tool gives suggestions and quality monitoring. if they want details, bring in SE or research.
[06:00] [Demo practice start] Priya Patel: launching demo — open the Redwood Console. show model selection, toggle dedicated vs hosted. show per-route dashboards.
[06:40] Priya Patel: ok, i'm going to run a generation against a 2k prompt, showing streaming output, note the p50/p95/p99 in the console.
[07:10] [Audio overlap] Alex Johnson: (talks over) call out when you switch to the fallback — maybe a line "if capacity constrained we automatically route to a compatible variant and keep your app online".
[07:40] Priya Patel: yeah, demo wording: "Redwood routes requests by policy (latency/cost/region) and has automatic fallbacks to keep apps alive".
[08:05] Lena Ortiz: can we have a short script for the fallback phrase? sellers stumble there.
[08:22] Alex Johnson: script phrase: "If capacity is limited we can automatically fail over to a compatible model variant or region, so your customers see graceful degradation instead of errors".
[08:45] Priya Patel: role-play scenario 1: enterprise fintech customer worried about latency and compliance — do it.
[09:10] Tom Nguyen (role-play as prospect): our priority is sub-200ms latency and SOC2 compliance, also we need control over keys.
[09:34] Priya Patel (as AE): under historic loads we hit p99 under 250ms on our dedicated tier and we support KMS/HSM for key control, also we can deploy private in your VPC or on-prem for auditability. would you consider starting with a short POC?
[10:05] Tom (as prospect): maybe, what's the price delta for dedicated vs hosted?
[10:20] Alex Johnson (whispers): handwave pricing, redirect to solutioning.
[10:25] Priya Patel: good question, we typically say dedicated has a predictable monthly commit with lower per-token costs at scale — we'll share the pricing grid.
[11:00] [Demo pause] Marcus Chen: quick note, mention batching/caching story: batching reduces per-token cost but can increase tail latency; caching prefixes reduces token computation for repeated prompts. don't say "K V cache" spelled out unless needed.
[11:40] Lena Ortiz: customers also ask about model rollouts — how to explain canary and A/B?
[11:55] Alex Johnson: explain rollouts: canary deploys, route percentage, automatic fallback policies and evaluation hooks that track regressions. tie to Optimize and Eval sets.
[12:22] Priya Patel: ok next role-play, competitive objection: "Why not just call OpenAI?"
[12:45] Elena Park (role-play): openai is simpler and probably cheaper for us right now.
[12:58] Priya Patel (as AE): acknowledge: "OpenAI is great for quick starts; where we help is when you need production reliability, private deployment, or predictable economics for high-volume use cases. we give you more deployment modes, observability, and cost controls".
[13:35] Tom Nguyen: mention performance per dollar and kernel-level optimizations — that's a real differentiator vs Anthropic and other smaller providers.
[14:00] Marcus Chen: add example: "we saw a customer reduce token cost by 30% with batching + prefix cache and switching to a quantized variant for some workloads" — don't use specific names unless public.
[14:30] Alex Johnson: good, capture that as a short case study line sellers can use.
[15:00] [Second demo run] Priya Patel: this time i'll simulate capacity constraint and show fallback to variant and route to different region. streaming will continue but latency bumps slightly.
[15:40] Priya Patel: live note: the console shows request trace and token-level cost, you can click to see which host served the request and fallback reason.
[16:05] Lena Ortiz: can AEs see per-token cost in the console?
[16:20] Marcus Chen: yes we show token-level cost, and the Optimize tool surfaces recommended configs to hit cost/latency targets.
[16:45] Alex Johnson: objection handling cheat: when they say "we're worried about vendor lock-in" — reply: "we support open models and the API is consistent across environments; you can pin model versions or run in your VPC".
[17:10] Priya Patel: ok now let's practice a security deep-dive micro-answer for AEs: short, mid, deep. short: "SOC2 ready, KMS, audit logs". mid: "we integrate with customer KMS/HSM, RBAC & audit logs, VPC/private deployment available". deep: "we'll loop in security team and share architecture and controls".
[17:55] Tom Nguyen: perfect. next, demo closing phrasing — how to ask for a pilot.
[18:10] Alex Johnson: script: "Would you be open to a 2-4 week pilot so we can validate latency and cost on your workload? We can run benchmarks and provide a rollout plan."
[18:28] Elena Park: role-play: prospect asks about legal and procurement lead time.
[18:40] Alex Johnson: answer: procurement can take 4-8 weeks for enterprise; expedite options exist for smaller pilots, and we have standard SOW and security docs to accelerate.
[19:05] [Cross-talk and small interruption] Sofia Alvarez: quick ask — can you highlight the one-pager bullets so trainers can put on a one-slide cheat sheet?
[19:22] Priya Patel: bullets: "Predictable latency/cost; Unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private; Smart routing & graceful fallbacks; Cost tools: batching, caching, quantization; Enterprise controls: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs, RBAC".
[20:00] Alex Johnson: ok role-play 3: handling price pushback with concrete numbers. try to avoid exact pricing unless asked — steer to commits/benchmarks.
[20:30] Tom Nguyen (role-play): "It's expensive".
[20:40] Priya Patel: "I understand. we recommend a short pilot so we can measure cost/latency on your actual prompts; often the combined effect of batching and quantization lowers unit cost enough to justify dedicated commits".
[21:05] Marcus Chen: also say: "we can instrument token-level costs and provide a forecast based on your usage patterns".
[21:30] Lena Ortiz: great, now let's timebox the practice demo and have each AE run a 5-min pitch. Elena first.
[21:45] Elena Park: (5-min pitch includes intro, 30-sec pitch, security line, demo snippet, ask for pilot)
[26:05] [Feedback] Alex Johnson: Elena, good energy, remember to slow down on the fallback explanation and use the script line.
[27:10] Raj Singh: my turn — run it quickly.
[32:00] [Feedback and notes] Priya Patel: Raj, good handle on the Optimize tool, but remember not to deep-dive into quantization unless asked.
[33:10] [Wrap-up role-play summaries] Alex Johnson: ok capture a few canned lines for the playbook: 1) 30s pitch, 2) fallback script, 3) security short/mid/deep, 4) pilot ask.
[33:40] Marcus Chen: also capture a short troubleshooting line: "if you see increased tail latency, check batching policy and prefix cache hit rates".
[34:10] Priya Patel: final mini demo: show how to flip to dedicated capacity in the console and the autoscaling/burst settings.
[35:00] [Questions from field] Tom Nguyen: what assets do we need to enable sellers?
[35:18] Sofia Alvarez: we need a one-page cheat sheet, updated demo script, 2 recorded demo runthroughs (basic + capacity constrained), and two role-play scenarios.
[35:45] Alex Johnson: ok we'll own the demo script and recordings. Priya will record. Alex will send the security and pricing docs. Lena will collect objections.
[36:10] [Recap and next steps] Alex Johnson: quick recap: Priya records demo, Alex shares security one-pager and pricing grid, Lena consolidates objections, Tom adds role-plays — meet back in 2 weeks.
[36:40] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[36:50] Alex Johnson: thanks all, end of session.
[36:55] [Recording ended — note: actual meeting lasted ~60 minutes; some sections abbreviated in transcript]
